name: Norfolk four-course crop rotation
description: East Anglian farmers used a rotation of cereal, root crop, cereal and clover or grasses to organize cropping.

impact.note: A rotation that removed fallow and reorganised farming around fodder crops in Britain and parts of Europe; a few later systems built on it.

date.label: Attested in some areas by the 1730s
date.basis: Wade Martins and Williamson report the Norfolk four-course in some areas from the 1730s; this is not a claim of regional or worldwide origin.

events.statement: The Norfolk four-course was attested in some East Anglian areas by the 1730s, according to the historians.

evidence.supports: The authors define the four-course and report that it was attested in some areas from the 1730s; other rotations remained widespread.

events.caveats: The 1730s attestation is a historian’s reconstruction, not a claim of invention or universal use; adoption varied substantially by farm and soil and the authors question a general yield advantage.
